classification.difficultyReason: Find landing coordinates for opposite launch directions and distinguish range from separation.

content.prompt: A ball is thrown at $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $60^\circ$. At the same time another ball is thrown from a point $30\text{ m}$ away, back towards the first, at $45^\circ$ and $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. How far apart do they land? Give your answer to 1 d.p. Use $g=10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

spec.description: Oppositely directed launches, crossing trajectories, speed and angle labels, and a dimension between launch points. Paths are plotted from the given equations; the second ball's apex is consequently slightly higher than the first, correcting the source schematic.
spec.mathematics: First trajectory y=sqrt(3)x-4x²/45 for 0≤x≤225sqrt(3)/20. Second trajectory y=(30-x)-(30-x)²/40 for -10≤x≤30. Launch points are x=0 and x=30.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied question figure without calculated landing coordinates or separation.

answer.worked:
Take the first launch point as $x=0$, with positive $x$ towards the second launch point.
For ball 1:
$$\begin{aligned}y_1&=15t\sin60^\circ-5t^2\\0&=t\left(\frac{15\sqrt3}{2}-5t\right)\\t_1&=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\text{ s}\\x_1&=15\cos60^\circ\left(\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\right)\\&=\frac{45\sqrt3}{4}\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
For ball 2, the horizontal velocity is negative:
$$\begin{aligned}y_2&=20t\sin45^\circ-5t^2\\0&=t(10\sqrt2-5t)\\t_2&=2\sqrt2\text{ s}\\x_2&=30-20\cos45^\circ(2\sqrt2)\\&=30-40\\&=-10\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
The distance between the landing points is
$$\begin{aligned}d&=\frac{45\sqrt3}{4}-(-10)\\&=10+\frac{45\sqrt3}{4}\\&\approx29.5\text{ m}.\end{aligned}$$
